title: Brain-spine interface restores volitional walking after cervical spinal cord injury (Lausanne, STIMO-BSI trial)
summary: Brain-spine interface let Gert-Jan Oskam, paralyzed since 2011, stand, walk and climb stairs by thought (Nature, May 2023)
account: In Lausanne's STIMO-BSI trial, a 38-year-old man (named in press as Gert-Jan Oskam) received two WIMAGINE 64-electrode cortical implants and a spinal paddle lead. He had an incomplete C5/C6 spinal cord injury from a cycling accident ten years earlier. A decoder trained on his cortical signals controlled spinal stimulation, letting him stand, walk, climb stairs and cross complex terrain. Performance stayed stable for over a year, including independent use at home. Lorach et al. reported in Nature on 24 May 2023 that he regained the ability to walk with crutches with the interface switched off. News reports place the implant surgery in 2021. As only the year is given, 1 January 2021 is used as the observation date.
purpose: Built to restore volitional control of leg movement after spinal cord injury by decoding movement intentions from cortical recordings and driving epidural spinal stimulation. Standing and walking were the intended benefit. The recovery of crutch-assisted walking with the interface switched off was a secondary finding the authors attribute to BSI-supported neurorehabilitation.
model_version: Two WIMAGINE 64-electrode epidural cortical implants (CEA-Clinatec) with a Specify 5-6-5 implantable paddle lead; Markov-switching multilinear decoder with REW-NPLS online calibration
developer: NeuroRestore (EPFL/CHUV/UNIL) with CEA-Clinatec and ONWARD Medical

ratings.reason: Life-changing benefit to one identifiable person: standing, walking, stair climbing and independent home use restored after ten years of paralysis. Some recovery persists when the device is switched off.

ai_role.statement: The AI is the decoder: a Hidden-Markov/multilinear model calibrated on the participant's cortical signals. It predicts intended movement and modulates stimulation amplitude in real time. The paper reports hip-muscle control within two minutes of calibration. Surgery and stimulation hardware are conventional. The walking benefit depends on the decoder translating intention into stimulation.

evidence.citation: Lorach H, Galvez A, Spagnolo V, et al. (2023). Walking naturally after spinal cord injury using a brain-spine interface. Nature. (Author affiliations include ONWARD Medical alongside EPFL/CHUV/UNIL and CEA Clinatec.)

produced_by: Incomplete cervical spinal cord injury with preserved cortical movement intention and residual lumbosacral circuits that epidural stimulation can recruit
Epidural cortical recording (WIMAGINE) paired with lumbosacral epidural stimulation, decoder calibrated to the individual
Supervised neurorehabilitation within a regulated feasibility trial (STIMO-BSI, NCT04632290)
must_hold: Decoder calibration remains fast and decoding performance stable over months
Spinal stimulation still recruits leg muscles (intact circuits below the lesion)
Participant can tolerate implanted hardware and use the wireless system independently

echoes.setting: CHUV, Lausanne; a further participant paralyzed from the waist down implanted with the ARC-BCI system (Clinatec WIMAGINE plus ONWARD ARC-IM) in a feasibility study
CHUV, Lausanne; two further participants (35-year-old woman, upper limb; 39-year-old man, lower limb), bringing the total to seven ARC-BCI implants
echoes.source: ONWARD Medical press release via BioSpace, 22 Jan 2026 (vendor-authored), https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/onward-medical-completes-two-additional-brain-computer-interface-implants-paired-with-spinal-cord-stimulation-technology-to-restore-thought-driven-movement

headline: Brain-spine interface lets Gert-Jan Oskam walk by thought
metric: performance stayed stable for over a year, including independent use at home

comparator.against: epidural spinal cord stimulation alone (STIMO), after which his recovery had plateaued for three years
comparator.before: after three years of regular training with stimulation only, he had reached a plateau of recovery; EES only condition showed significantly shorter step length due to increase of failed steps; WISCI II score 6 before STIMO
comparator.after: the BSI enabled walking with gait features that were markedly closer to those quantified in healthy individuals; WISCI II 16 after STIMO-BSI
comparator.quote: Compared to stimulation alone, the BSI enabled walking with gait features that were markedly closer to those quantified in healthy individuals (Extended Data Fig. 4a). The BSI ensured a continuous link between the intended movement and the modulation of stimulation protocols, which translated into the ability to walk overground

later.note: ONWARD Medical implanted a second participant with the WIMAGINE plus ARC-IM brain-computer interface at CHUV in the same Lausanne feasibility program.
later.quote: Onward Medical has successfully implanted a second patient with a brain-computer interface (BCI) system to restore lower limb movement.
